intro: One adverbial relation, several syntactic shapes: a subordinate clause with the verb at the end (weil, da, obwohl, damit, ohne dass, falls), a main clause with a coordinating conjunction (denn, sondern) or a linking adverb in position 1 (deshalb, trotzdem, sonst, danach), an infinitive clause (um … zu, ohne … zu, statt … zu, zu … um zu, genug, um zu), a verb-first conditional (Hast du Zeit, …), the literary kaum … da, and occasionally a preposition (trotz, bei). Each of the 21 items gives you the source sentence and a target frame; the gap is only the part that carries the change: the connector, the preposition, or the infinitive construction. The rest of the target is printed, so the word order in the frame tells you which kind of word is needed.
tips[0].title: Conjunction, subordinator or adverb: watch the verb
tips[0].text: Coordinating conjunctions (denn, aber, sondern, und, oder) stand outside the clause: the verb stays in second position (…, denn er war krank). Subordinating conjunctions (weil, da, obwohl, damit, falls, nachdem) send the verb to the end (…, da er krank war). Linking adverbs (deshalb, daher, trotzdem, dennoch, sonst, danach) occupy position 1 themselves, so the verb follows immediately (…; deshalb blieb er). da is always subordinating in this sense: it belongs with weil, not with denn.
tips[0].trap: Not *…, denn war er krank*: after denn the subject comes first. And not *…, deshalb er blieb*: after a linking adverb the verb comes next.
tips[0].check.why: The subject comes right after the gap and the verb is second: only coordinating denn fits that order.
tips[1].title: Compressing into an infinitive: same subject only
tips[1].text: damit ↔ um … zu, ohne dass ↔ ohne … zu, statt dass ↔ statt … zu work only when both clauses share the subject. With a new subject the dass-clause (or damit) must stay: Er sprach langsam, damit man ihn verstand. Past actions become a perfect infinitive: ohne ihn gelesen zu haben ↔ ohne dass sie ihn gelesen hatte. The negative consequence has its own compressed form: so leise, dass niemand ihn verstand ↔ zu leise, um verstanden zu werden; its positive twin is genug, um … zu.
tips[1].trap: Not *Sie sparte, um ihr Sohn zu studieren*: different subjects need damit.
tips[1].check.why: The subjects differ (er / seine Tochter), so no infinitive clause is possible; damit keeps the purpose clause.
tips[2].title: Condition and time: the special shapes
tips[2].text: A conditional clause can drop wenn and put the verb first: Hast du Zeit, (dann) komm vorbei. The formal version is Sollten Sie Fragen haben, … . A negative condition becomes an imperative plus sonst / andernfalls. For sudden succession, literary German uses kaum with verb-first and an optional da: Kaum war er angekommen, da rief er an. A sequence with nachdem can also be split into two main clauses with danach or anschließend.
tips[2].trap: After the kaum-clause the verb comes first or follows da: not *Kaum war er angekommen, er rief an*.
tips[2].check.why: The kaum-clause is verb-first, and the main clause puts its verb right after da (or first).
tips[3].title: Argue in subordinates, narrate in mains, compress in infinitives
tips[3].text: An argument makes the logic explicit with weil, obwohl, damit. A narrative keeps the pace with main clauses and adverbs: deshalb, trotzdem, danach, kaum … da. A formal or dense sentence compresses with um … zu, ohne … zu, or a preposition (trotz, bei). Choose the shape for the text type; vary them for style.
tips[3].check.why: A concession compresses into trotz + genitive; wegen would turn it into a cause.
remember[0]: denn / sondern: verb second; weil / da / obwohl: verb last; deshalb / trotzdem / sonst: verb right after the adverb.
remember[1]: um … zu, ohne … zu, statt … zu only with the same subject.
remember[2]: so … dass nicht ↔ zu … um zu; so … dass ↔ genug, um zu.
remember[3]: Hast du Zeit, …; Sollten Sie …; Kaum war er da, da …

mistakes[0].why: denn is coordinating: subject first, verb second.
mistakes[1].why: The infinitive clause needs the same subject; a new subject needs damit.
mistakes[2].why: After the kaum-clause the verb comes first, or right after da.
mistakes[3].why: da in the causal sense is a subordinating conjunction, not a linking adverb.
hook: Say 'because', 'although' or 'in order to' in three different shapes and pick the one that suits your text.
